一.title: The Teacher
paragraphs: The story begins with a teacher. In the 1980s, Koos van Wezel taught judo with great passion in Tholen, Roosendaal and Scherpenisse. He was a pupil of Haku Michigami — the very master who also shaped Anton Geesink. That bond with tradition would give the club its name and its soul.

In 1993, Koos turned that passion into something lasting: together with his son Erwin van Wezel and Marinus Smout, he founded Judoclub Michigami — officially established in Nieuw-Vossemeer, with the dojo in Sportcentrum De Knotwilg in Steenbergen, as a tribute to his teacher. A small dojo, a handful of judoka, and the conviction that judo is more than a sport: it is a way of life.

二.title: The Golden Years
paragraphs: The nineties and the noughties were the club's flowering. The dojo was a buzzing place where judo was spoken like a second language: two training groups on Thursdays, three on Fridays. Koos also taught in Nieuw-Vossemeer and Scherpenisse, and the club built a broad foundation right across the region. Michigami was one of the largest clubs in the region — and remained so throughout the noughties.

The club lived beyond the mat as well. Koos's son Erwin was active in those years himself and taught from time to time, his wife Els always supported the club, and daughter Jolanda was a constant presence. Jolanda married Franco Hack — together they had three sons, among them the twins Robin and Pascal. Both boys were on the mat as children, and would later become the board and the coaches of Michigami. And then there was Alex van Loon, who assisted Koos at training for years — an indispensable second hand behind the mat.

The competition squad travelled to the great tournaments in London and Paris every year. Each year, the outing to Pony Park Slagharen was a highlight, where judoka could spar with leading figures such as Anton Geesink himself. In those days the region teemed with judo — and Michigami was one of its engines.
二.photoCaption: Annual training camp in Slagharen — photographed with Anton Geesink

三.title: The New Generation
paragraphs: Around 2010 a new phase began. Robin Hack, Pascal Hack and Robert Dingenouts — with the club since almost its founding — began teaching alongside their own training, under the guidance of Koos. On 5 June 2010 they all passed their 1st Dan, in 2014 the 2nd Dan and in 2016 the 3rd Dan. Wendy Jansen, who had started with Koos in Tholen in 1988, was also a constant presence in the club — she would go on to earn her black belt in 2024.
三.photoCaption: After passing the 2nd Dan — from left to right: Robert, Pascal, Koos and Robin

四.title: The Quieter Years
paragraphs: From the mid-2010s things gradually grew quieter. It was a slow process: there were fewer competition judoka, which made tournaments harder to organise. The membership shrank, and clubs were disappearing from the region. The region that had teemed with judo in the nineties and noughties was quietly growing smaller.

五.title: The Final Blow
paragraphs: The coronavirus crisis (2020–2021) was the final blow. Training stood still for months, and many clubs in the region went under. Michigami barely managed to stay on its feet — and from that moment the club worked hard to grow and improve again.

In December 2021, Koos van Wezel died at far too young an age. The dojo held its breath, but the spirit held firm: Robin, Pascal and Robert — who had been teaching alongside Koos for years — took on full leadership and kept the flame of Michigami alive.

六.title: A Minute of Silence
paragraphs: The year 2026 brought a loss that cut deep: on 28 March, Franco Hack — Koos's son-in-law, father of Robin and Pascal — died at just 59 years of age. Franco was a fourth dan and a familiar face at Michigami: he trained many of the members on their way to their black belt, practised kata's with them, and at dan examinations he served as uke for several judoka. He was a wonderful sparring partner — especially in ne-waza. Together with Jolanda he sat behind the jury table at countless tournaments, and as a coach he was there when Robert, Robin and Pascal saw action internationally, as at the CSIT in Grenoble.

On 1 April 2026 the club observed a minute of silence for him in Steenbergen and in Oud-Vossemeer: seated around the mat, silent, together. A judoka for life, who carried on Koos's path with the same gentle hand.

七.title: Two Locations, One Club
paragraphs: The hard work paid off. Michigami is once again a thriving club: from toddlers to adults, recreational or competitive. In 2024 the dojo in Steenbergen expanded with new 120 m² mats — permanently laid, ready for the club and for the associations that share the hall — and Robin and Pascal taught in Oud-Vossemeer, a location that now firmly belongs to the club.

In October 2026, OVJV (Oud-Vossemeerse Judo Vereniging) celebrates its 50th anniversary — a milestone that Michigami proudly shares in. The board of OVJV asked Michigami to take over the association. 2026 is the transition year: in 2027 the integration will be complete, and OVJV will cease to exist as an independent association. From then on: two locations, one club.
With a warm atmosphere and a committed community, the club looks to the future with confidence, ready to inspire many more generations along the gentle way.
